previous_findings.note: A PRE_ATTEMPT mount now carries only its V0 stage group, with no <title> or <desc> and a situation-only aria-label ('The trolley'). All 22 Core2A, 16 Core2B and 11 Core1B pre-attempt SVGs checked in the DOM: exactly one stage group, no title, desc, aria-labelledby or title attribute. The full <desc> is only on the POST_ATTEMPT mount inside the locked disclosure.

No pre-attempt figure has a result-bearing tooltip or accessible name any more. The labels are neutral: 'The lift', 'The wedge', 'The stack', 'Two trials' and so on. The result-bearing titles now sit only on the post-attempt mounts.

In all 11 Core1B units, 'Your answer should contain', the reconstruct prompts and the model response now rebuild the task the learner attempted: the car at 25 m/s, the 3 kg box on a string, the man in the boat, the braking train, the braking car, the block on the wall, the rocket, the 5 kg box, the car and trailer, the two carts, and the pulley at y_A = 0.6 m.

Each Core1B unit now mounts a figure of its own attempt, for example REP-NLM-BOX5-PUSH-30N-PRESS-20N, REP-NLM-CAR-BRAKING-1200KG and REP-NLM-ROCKET-EXHAUST-5000N. The figure is situation-only before the attempt and staged with this task's values after it.

The task was re-authored: μ_s = 0.75, the smallest starting pull horizontally, at 37° and at 53°, against a 61 N worker. Re-derived: P = 75/(cos θ + 0.75 sin θ) gives 75 N, 60 N and 62.5 N, so only the 37° pull works. transfer.novelty now cites the Core1B FRICTION-QUANT attempt, and the demand (an unknown pull whose direction is the choice) is new. The figure was not updated; that is filed as a new S1.
Rung 4 now reads 'Write the friction rest needs and the most the contact can give … Which of the two must not exceed the other?'. It no longer states the inequality, and rung 5 only simplifies it.
The h1, <title> and breadcrumb now read 'Newton's first law and free-body diagrams', which is learner-facing. That this title is narrower than the product's scope is filed separately as S3.

FRAME-CHOICE-07 is now a new instance: an apple dropped from 1.25 m in a van accelerating at 2 m/s² lands 0.25 m behind the mark, re-derived. FIXED-PULLEY-04 is a new instance too: a cart on a table, x + y = 1.4 m, x = 0.1 m, dy/dt = +0.3 m/s and d²y/dt² = +1.2 m/s², re-derived.
Core1A FBD-BODY-OWNERSHIP now mounts REP-NLM-CHILD-ON-BOX (200 N, 500 N, 700 N). FRAME-CHOICE now mounts REP-NLM-LIFT-SCALE-60KG, where N = 720 N in both frames.

The answer and failure signal now both say 'drawn three times'. The post-attempt figure title ('a diagram that counts gravity twice'), its stage-2 <desc> ('counts it twice') and the pre-attempt caption ('so the double count is diagnosed') still disagree with them. Re-filed below.
Each option label is now printed once ('(A) … (B) …'), on all 13 source items.
'abc' still unlocks a unit. Page search still singles out an item from text inside its locked answer. The wedge label still overprints. Re-filed below.

findings.detail: The task was re-authored but its figure REP-NLM-CRATE10-TWO-PULLS (safe_ref = bound_ref) still draws the previous task, with values that contradict the stem. Before the attempt the learner sees '10 kg crate: a 50 N pull, horizontal and then at 37°', 'μ_s = 0.55, μ_k = 0.40' and 'slipping not stated'. The stem says μ_s = 0.75, gives no pull (the pull is the unknown) and asks about three directions, including 53°, which the figure never shows. After the attempt, the staged figure narrates the old solution ('Trial 2: N = 100 − 30 = 70 N, limit 38.5 N, need 40 N … slides … a = 1.2 m/s²'). The answer directly above it is 75 N / 60 N / 62.5 N. So the pre-attempt representation misstates the given coefficient, and the post-attempt representation contradicts the answer. Replace it with a figure of this task: a 10 kg crate on a floor with μ_s = 0.75 and a rope at 0°, 37° and 53°, the pull P unknown, and the 61 N worker limit. After the attempt, stage N = 100 − P sin θ, P cos θ = 0.75 N, and the thresholds 75 N, 60 N and 62.5 N.

Core1 figures do not depict their own compact anchor. Only 3 of 11 Core1 units mount a figure, and each is a qualitative representation without values. FRAME-CHOICE draws a person on a scale in a lift ('v down, a up'), but its compact anchor is a 2 kg bag on the floor of a van accelerating at 3 m/s², pseudo-force 6 N backward. FRICTION-QUANT draws a crate pulled at an angle θ above the horizontal, but its anchor is a 2 kg block pulled horizontally with 14 N (μ_s 0.5 → limit 10 N, slides, f_k = 6 N, a = 4 m/s²). FBD-BODY-OWNERSHIP draws the horse and cart qualitatively, while its anchor has the numbers (200 kg cart, 600 N pull, 200 N friction, a = 2 m/s²). Mount, or draw, the anchor's own situation with its values: the van and bag with a 6 N backward pseudo-force; the 2 kg block with 14 N against a 10 N limit; the cart with 600 N and 200 N.

The independent check is false. It reads 'Switch the chosen body to the fridge door: the four partner arrows now appear on its diagram'. One of the four partners, the magnet's 1 N gravitational pull on the Earth, acts on the Earth, as the item's own answer says. Only three partners (3 N magnetic pull on the fridge, 3 N push into the door, 1 N friction drag on the door surface) appear on the door's diagram. Correct wording: 'Switch to the fridge door: three partner arrows (3 N toward the magnet, 3 N into the door, 1 N down along it) now appear on its diagram; the fourth, 1 N up, is on the Earth's.'

The stem says 'A block rests on a smooth fixed incline', with gravity and the normal force as the only interactions. That state is impossible: with no friction, mg sin θ is unbalanced and the block accelerates down the plane at g sin θ. The figure <desc> repeats 'rests'. Say 'A block slides down a smooth fixed incline' (or 'is held on'). The count wording is also still split: answer and failure signal say 'drawn three times', but the post-attempt figure title says 'a diagram that counts gravity twice', stage 2 says 'the diagram counts it twice', and the pre-attempt caption says 'the double count'. Use 'the weight is drawn three times: once as mg and again as its two components' throughout (ILLUSTRATOR for the figure text).
An internal code reaches the learner. The boundary answer ends 'switching the body switches the inventory (NLM3-3).' Remove '(NLM3-3)'.

Rung 3 does not climb past rung 2. Rung 2 already says 'mark which way the crate would slide relative to the bed if the bed were slippery'. Rung 3 repeats it ('Imagine the bed perfectly slippery: which way would the crate slide relative to the bed? Friction on the crate opposes that'). A climbing rung 3: 'The crate slows with the truck at 3 m/s². Which single horizontal force gives it that acceleration, and what F = ma does it need?'

Two pre-attempt captions (visible before any attempt) tell the learner the count the stem asks them to find. COV-03 asks for 'every force on the magnet', and its caption reads 'Show the magnet on the vertical door with its four forces…'. COV-06's caption reads '…the book on the table with its two forces and each force's third-law partner…'. Use situation-only captions before the attempt, e.g. 'Show the magnet held on the vertical steel door.'

The title is now learner-facing: 'Newton's first law and free-body diagrams'. It names only the first of 11 microtopics, though. The product also teaches F = ma, third-law pairs, static and kinetic friction, connected bodies, ideal strings and pulleys, inclines and accelerating frames. A learner looking for 'friction' or 'pulleys' will not find them from the title. Use 'Force and laws of motion' or 'Newton's laws of motion'.

Still open. Gating holds in Chromium. Across core1a (11), core1b (22), core2 (13), core2a (22) and core2b (16), none of the 84 gated disclosures opened on click, Enter or Space without an attempt. An empty or whitespace attempt does not unlock. Hints reveal one rung per click (1 → 2 → 3, then 'Next hint' is disabled). Stage stepping, the display panel (dark theme, zoom 1.1) and Home (../../../index.html, which exists in public/) work, and no page has JS errors or horizontal overflow. But any 3 characters ('abc') unlock a unit. The search still filters on article.textContent, which includes locked answers and post-attempt <desc>: typing '62.5' shows only Q-PHY-NLM-2B-FRICTION-STATE-01, and '0.25' only Q-PHY-NLM-2A-FRAME-CHOICE-07. The wedge figure of Q-PHY-NLM-INCLINE-2B-COMPONENT-TRAP-04 still overprints 'block on wedge: 17.3 N' on the '5 kg' label (measured bounding-box overlap; confirmed on screenshot). In the Core1A NET-ZERO-MOTION puck figure, the stage-1 note 'stick has lost contact; friction and air resistance negligible' runs into the stage-3 text 'still 4 m/s at 3 s, 12 m covered'.
